author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Russian strike hit a petrol station complex in southwestern Kyiv early Thursday, injuring four people and setting off fires, Ukrainian officials said.

Reuters reported that the attack marked the first time a petrol station had been struck in the Ukrainian capital during the war. Images from the scene showed heavy damage, including at least one destroyed vehicle. Fire also spread to a neighboring building before emergency crews worked to contain it.

The strike came during another night of drone attacks on Kyiv. The city has faced an almost continuous barrage of jet-powered drones for nearly two weeks, increasing pressure on air defenses and emergency services. Officials were still assessing the full damage and did not immediately provide detailed information about the condition of those injured.

Claims and casualty figures in an active conflict can change as responders search damaged areas and authorities verify reports. The core facts in this article are attributed to Ukrainian officials and Reuters reporting available Thursday morning. The attack remains a developing story, with additional information expected from Kyiv’s emergency and military authorities.
dek: Emergency crews responded after an overnight attack ignited a fuel complex in southwestern Kyiv, as the city endured another wave of Russian drones.
headline: Russian strike hits Kyiv petrol station and injures four
